Stage 5 · Grammar

Grammar

Can I…? Could you…? — polite requests.
Track 3.17 — two requests, two repliesOriginal coursebook recording
Show transcript
1 Can I sit here, please? — Of course you can. 2 Could I leave early tomorrow? — I'm sorry, but that's not possible.
1Can I sit here, please? —
2Could I leave early tomorrow? —
Why

Yes → Of course you can. No → I'm sorry, but that's not possible.

In other words
“Excuse me. Could I open the window?” — “Yes, of course.”
“Can you repeat that, please?” — “Sure.”
“Can we leave our bags here?” — “I'm afraid not.”
“Could I leave early tomorrow?” — “I'm sorry, but that's not possible.”
Notice

Notice: who does the action in “Can I…?” — and in “Can you…?”

You want to…AskReply
do something yourselfCan I sit here? · Could I open the window?Of course you can. / I'm afraid not.
ask another person to do itCan you repeat that? · Could you sign here, please?Sure. / I'm sorry, but that's not possible.
offer somethingWould you like a coffee?Yes, please. / No, thank you.
In other words
Can I…? = I want to do it. Can you…? = I want YOU to do it.
Could is the same — just more polite. Add please at the end.
Saying no politely: “I'm afraid not.” · “I'm sorry, but that's not possible.” — never just “No!”
After Can/Could — base verb: “Could you help me?” (not “to help”).
Notice

Notice: who does the action in “Can I…?” — and in “Can you…?” Tell your partner.

In other words
Can I…? = I do it. Can you…? = you do it. Could = more polite.
Saying no politely: “I'm afraid not.” · “I'm sorry, but that's not possible.”
Notice

Notice: who does the action in “Can I…?” — and in “Can you…?” Tell your teacher.

In other words
Can I…? = I do it. Can you…? = you do it. Could = more polite.
Saying no politely: “I'm afraid not.” · “I'm sorry, but that's not possible.”
Stage 6 · Practice

Practice

Part 1 — Can I or Can you?
1___ open the window? It's hot. (I want to do it)
2___ help me with this box, please? (you do it)
3___ borrow your phone for a minute?
4___ sign here, please?
5___ send you the details by email?
6___ call me back after lunch?
Why

I do it → Can/Could I. You do it → Can/Could you.

1❌ “Could you to help me?”
2❌ “Can I lend your pen?” (you want to take it)
3❌ “Would you like come to dinner?”
Why

Could you help (base verb) · you take → borrow · Would you like to come.

1“Could I send them by email later?” —
2“Can we leave our bags here?” —
3“Can you repeat that, please?” —
4I can swim, but I ___ ride a bike.
Why

That's fine · I'm afraid not · Sure. And can → can't for the negative.

1___ borrow your dictionary? (I take it)
2___ pass the sugar, please? (you do it)
3___ book the restaurant for Friday? (you do it)
4___ send you my answer tomorrow? (I do it)
Why

I do it → Can/Could I. You do it → Can/Could you.

1❌ “Could you to print this?”
2❌ “Can you borrow me €10?”
3❌ “Would you like a coffee? — Yes, I like.”
Why

Could you print · you give → lend · offer → Yes, please.

1“Can we use the computers after class?” —
2“Could you give me my money back?” —
3He can cook, but he ___ drive.
Why

Polite yes/no replies · can → can't.

1___ borrow your dictionary? (I take it)
2___ pass the sugar, please? (you do it)
3___ book the restaurant for Friday? (you do it)
4___ send you my answer tomorrow? (I do it)
Why

I do it → Can/Could I. You do it → Can/Could you.

2❌ “Can you borrow me €10?”

Stage 7 · Listen

Listen

Track 3.15 — the first classOriginal coursebook recording
Show transcript
A: Hello and welcome, everyone. Before we begin, I'd like to tell you a few things about the course. B: Excuse me. Could I open the window? A: Yes, of course. It's really hot in here, isn't it? So… class is at 2 p.m. every Thursday and Friday in the room next door. You can use the computers there… Yes, do you have a question? C: Er, yes… Can we use the computers after class? A: Yes, of course, but you need a password. It's 'student451'. C: Sorry, can you repeat that, please? B: Sure. It's student451. That's S-T-U-D-E-N-T-4-5-1. B: And can we leave our books and bags in the computer room? A: I'm afraid not. There are evening classes in that room from 6 p.m. Now, if there's nothing else… Oh, before you leave today, could you give your personal details to the administrator, please? C: Sorry, but I don't have them with me today. Could I send them by email later? A: That's fine. Just tell the administrator before you leave.
The first class of a course — full of requests.

Listen once. Then answer the questions.

1Why does the student open the window?
2What is the computer password?
3Can they leave their bags in the computer room?
4What does one student want to send by email?
Why

It's hot → the window · password student451 · bags: I'm afraid not · he sends his personal details later.

Stage 8 · Email

Email

Write a short email to your teacher or boss with two requests.

Open politely, ask with Could I / Could you, close politely.

Useful language
  • Dear… / Hi…
  • Thanks for your email.
  • Could I…?
  • Could you…?
  • Best wishes,
  • Kind regards,
Four situations where you have to ask.

Each person knows only their own goal. Then swap.

Useful language
  • Excuse me, could I…?
  • Could you…, please?
  • Of course you can.
  • I'm afraid not.
  • I'm sorry, but that's not possible.
  • Thanks a lot!
Four situations where you have to ask.

Each person knows only their own goal. Then swap roles.

Useful language
  • Excuse me, could I…?
  • Could you…, please?
  • Of course you can.
  • I'm afraid not.
  • I'm sorry, but that's not possible.
  • Thanks a lot!
In other words
Round 1 — at work. Student A: you want to leave early tomorrow AND borrow the office laptop. Student B: you are the boss — say yes to only ONE request.
Round 2 — with a neighbour. Student B: you go on holiday — you want your neighbour to water your plants AND lend you a big bag. Student A: you are the neighbour — one yes, one no, politely.
Swap roles for each round. The second time is where the language sticks.

Stage 9 · Type it

Type it

Now produce it — type, don’t tap.

Spelling counts. Type the answers, then check.

1___ you help me, please? (polite)
2___ I borrow your pen?
3I'm afraid I ___ help you today. (negative)
Why

Could I/you + base verb + please \u00b7 never 'Could you TO help'.

1Could you to help me?
2Can I borrowing your pen?
3I am afraid I can't helps you.
Why

Could I/you + base verb + please \u00b7 never 'Could you TO help'.

1Make it polite: Give me your pen.
2Make it polite: I want to use your phone.
3Make it polite: Close the window.
Why

Could I/you + base verb + please \u00b7 never 'Could you TO help'.
